Testimony of Senator Anne Carney introducing
LD 983, "An Act Regarding Service of Notice of Restricted Person Status to
Hospitalized Patients," before the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary
March 24, 2025
Representative Kuhn and esteemed colleagues on the Committee on Judiciary, I am Senator
Anne Carney, proudly representing Senate District 29, which includes South Portland, Cape
Elizabeth and part of Scarborough. It is a pleasure to be with you to introduce LD 983, "An Act
Regarding Service of Notice of Restricted Person Status to Hospitalized Patients."
This bill addresses a situation that presents challenges to both hospitals and law enforcement agencies by creating a cooperative process for law enforcement to serve notice of orders under
Maine's yellow flag law when the defendant to be served is in a hospital setting.
The proposed statute outlines a process for law enforcement to request that a hospital provide
access to a defendant who is receiving care in the hospital for purposes of serving an extreme
risk protection order. This bill adds a process to the cooperation statute for law enforcement to request access to a hospitalized patient for purpose of serving notice of restricted person status
that is similar to the process used to serve an order under Maine's Protection From Abuse Act. Hospitals request this change so that the law applies the same standard to their work with law
enforcement in these two similar situations.
Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to introduce this bill. Representatives from Maine's hospitals will be following my testimony to provide additional information.
Anne Carney
State Senator, District 29

Testimony of Jim Bailinson, MaineHealth In Support of LD 983, "An Act Regarding Service of Notice of Restricted
Person Status to Hospitalized Patients" March 24, 2025
Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary, I am Jim Bailinson, Corporate Counsel at MaineHealth, and I am here on behalf of MaineHealth in support LD 983, "An Act Regarding Service of Notice of Restricted Person Status to Hospitalized Patients."
MaineHealth is an integrated non-profit health care system that provides a continuum of health care services to communities throughout Maine and New Hampshire. Every day, our over 24,000 care team members support our vision of "Working Together so Our Communities are the Healthiest in America" by providing a range of services from primary and specialty physician services to a continuum of behavioral health care services, community and tertiary hospital care, home health care and a lab.
MaineHealth recognizes the important role of the weapons restriction order process and works cooperatively with law enforcement in these situations consistent with the requirements of patient rights and confidentiality laws. There have been recent instances, however, where law enforcement had difficulty serving weapons restriction orders on hospitalized patients due to patient confidentiality laws, and LD 983 seeks to clarify hospitals' responsibilities regarding cooperation with law enforcement for purposes of restricted person notice.
I'd like to provide a few examples of where the existing law has created confusion. Recently, a patient had been placed on restricted or confidential status in the hospital directory, which is their right. We can only confirm the patient's presence in the hospital to people who are informed of their restricted status and given a code word to be able to access them. In another case, a patient was on a behavioral health unit where to protect patient privacy we do not acknowledge their presence to those who inquire. In both these cases, the court orders were eventually served on the patients once the relevant hospital personnel were contacted by law enforcement.
LD 983 will confirm that patient rights are not violated by allowing service of the court orders in these circumstances and will remove a level of confusion over this process.
Thank you and I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.

In general law enforcement becomes aware that an individual they are seeking to serve notice on is hospitalized through law enforcement presence in the emergency

follows:

B. A hospital may disclose that the person is a patient to facilitate notice under this

Testimony of Major Tyler Stevenson Maine State Police
In Support of (983)
An Act Regarding Service of Notice of Restricted Person Status to Hospitalized Patients.
Sponsored by Senator Carney Committee on Judiciary
Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and honorable members of the Committee on Judiciary: My name is Major Tyler Stevenson, and I am providing testimony on behalf of the Maine State Police and the Maine Department of Public Safety to testify in support of LD 983, "An Act Regarding Service of Notice of Restricted Person Status to Hospitalized Patients."
This bill aims to provide authorization to law enforcement to access a patient in a hospital to make notification to the patient that they are restricted person resulting from an extreme risk protection order.
As of mid-March 2025, the Maine State Police has executed 67 extreme risk protection orders since the inception of the law. The process to complete an extreme risk protection order requires an officer to take a person into protective custody when the officer has probable cause to believe the person may be mentally ill and presents a likelihood of serious harm because the person possesses, controls or may acquire a dangerous weapon. Typically, once in protective custody, the officer transports the person to a medical facility for an evaluation. If the assessment of a medical practitioner finds that the person presents a likeness of foreseeable harm the officer shall present the information to a Justic or a Judge for endorsement. If endorsed, the officer shall notify the person as soon as practicable that they are restricted from possessing, attempting to possess dangerous weapons. The person is not restricted from possessing dangerous weapons until they are notified.
The relationship between law enforcement and medical facilities varies from facility to facility and staff to staff. In most cases the extreme risk protection order process is seamless and efficient. However, the Maine State Police has encountered complications with hospital staff on a few occasions. Troopers have been asked to leave the exam room the person is being held in, which would have prevented the person from being accessed by a medical practitioner via telehealth. On another occasion, Troopers were asked to leave the hospital altogether and began to work on the extreme risk protection order process. While completing the process the person was released from the hospital without any notification to the Troopers. This prevented the Troopers from making notification to the person in a timely manner.
